About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The Manager – Markets
is responsible for leading and managing all municipal market operations within NCDC, ensuring markets operate as safe, clean, orderly, and accessible trading environments. The role oversees vendor management, revenue collection, infrastructure maintenance, and stakeholder engagement while driving improvements in market systems and service delivery. It plays a key role in supporting local economic activity, food security, and inclusive participation, particularly for women, youth, and small-scale traders.
Role Purpose
The role exists to provide strategic and operational leadership in the management of NCDC markets, ensuring compliance with health, safety, and regulatory standards while delivering efficient, transparent, and inclusive market services. Through effective coordination, governance, and stakeholder engagement, the Manager supports sustainable market operations, improved vendor livelihoods, and safe public trading spaces.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and manage daily operations of all NCDC municipal markets
Ensure compliance with health, safety, and regulatory standards
Oversee vendor registration, stall allocation, and vendor relations
Manage revenue collection systems and ensure financial accountability
Monitor and maintain market infrastructure, cleanliness, and functionality
Coordinate contractor performance (cleaning, security, maintenance)
Promote safe and inclusive trading environments for all users
Engage with vendors, communities, and stakeholders to improve services
Monitor performance and prepare operational and financial reports
Support emergency response and incident management within markets
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Public Administration, Economics, Community Development, or a related field
Preferred:
Other certifications and training, or a postgraduate qualifications relevant to the role.
Driver’s License (minimum Class 3).
Skills & Knowledge
Strong leadership and team management with the ability to drive performance across multiple market sites
Sound understanding of market operations, vendor management, and community-based economic activities
Knowledge of public health, sanitation, safety regulations, and municipal by-laws
Strong financial management capability, including revenue collection, budgeting, and procurement processes
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships with vendors, communities, and partners
Strong organisational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities
Ability to analyse operational challenges and implement practical, sustainable improvements
Understanding of community engagement approaches and inclusive service delivery practices
Work Experience
Demonstrated more than 5 years’ experience in managing operational service environments such as markets, facilities, community services, or similar public service operations.
Experience supervising staff and coordinating service delivery across multiple locations or teams.
Experience working with community stakeholders, vendors, or small business operators.
Experience managing operational budgets, revenue collection systems, or contractor services.
Experience working with government agencies, development partners, or community organisations is desirable.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
If you are passionate about data-driven decision-making and city transformation, we encourage you to apply.
How to Apply
Interested candidates are encouraged to:
Review the available roles and position requirements
Prepare to upload relevant supporting documentation
Cover Letter
Up-to-date CV, include in the one file along with your CV: copies of educational qualifications and a copy of a valid driver's licence (if applicable)
Click on the "APPLY NOW" button and submit an application through the Peopleconnexion PNG application portal.
Open to Port Moresby residents only.
Due to volume of candidates, only short-listed candidates will be contacted regarding applicant progress.
Applications are assessed on merit, capability, and alignment with NCDC’s values and service mandate.
Be part of the team shaping the future of Port Moresby — apply today.
Apply

The Manager - Parks & Open Spaces
oversees the planning, development, maintenance, and management of all public parks, open spaces, and recreational areas within NCD. The role ensures high-quality, safe, and accessible outdoor spaces while managing staff, contractors, and community groups to deliver projects and programs efficiently. By implementing sustainable and community-focused initiatives, the Manager supports NCDC’s environmental and social objectives.

This position exists to provide strategic leadership and operational management for NCD’s parks and open spaces. It ensures that public areas are maintained to high standards, community needs are met, and environmental and sustainability goals are achieved through effective planning, resource allocation, and stakeholder engagement.

Provide leadership, direction, and strategic planning for parks, gardens, roadside greenery, and recreational facilities.
Oversee the planning, implementation, and evaluation of projects, beautification programs, and community engagement initiatives.
Manage horticultural maintenance, including supervision of contractors, staff, and use of equipment and machinery.
Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and regulatory standards across all parks and open spaces.
Develop and monitor budgets, implement cost-control measures, and report on financial performance.
Engage with internal and external stakeholders, community groups, schools, and development partners to support collaborative initiatives.
Promote sustainable practices, including water conservation, native planting, and waste reduction.
Maintain accurate records, documentation, and reporting systems for activities, inspections, and projects.

Must hold a Driver’s License (minimum Class 3).

Strong leadership and strategic planning skills for managing staff and resources effectively.
Knowledge of horticulture, parks management, and environmental sustainability practices.
Experience in project planning, execution, and evaluation, including budgeting and resource allocation.
Understanding of regulatory compliance, health, safety, and environmental legislation.
Ability to foster community engagement and manage stakeholder relationships.
Excellent organisational, reporting, and documentation skills.
Capacity to manage operations in both office and outdoor environments under varying conditions.
Problem-solving skills to address challenges such as vandalism, aging infrastructure, and budget constraints.

At least 5 years of experience in Parks, Open Spaces and recreational area management or related fields

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.

The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The Assistant Planner
supports the Physical Planner (Development Control) in delivering NCDC’s physical planning initiatives, ensuring compliance with land use, zoning, building, and infrastructure regulations. The role assists in assessing planning applications, conducting site inspections, investigating complaints, and engaging with stakeholders. It plays a key role in facilitating orderly urban development, infrastructure planning, and sustainable land management while supporting efficient municipal operations.
Role Purpose
The role exists to provide operational and technical support in implementing physical planning projects, ensuring that all planning applications, inspections, and investigations meet regulatory standards. By maintaining accurate records, supporting policy implementation, and liaising with stakeholders, the Assistant Planner contributes to well-organized, compliant, and sustainable urban and infrastructure development in the National Capital District.
Key Responsibilities
Assess and screen physical planning applications to ensure compliance with NCDC regulations, building codes, and land use legislation.
Conduct routine inspections of residential, commercial, and industrial sites to monitor compliance with planning, building, and licensing standards.
Investigate complaints and incidents related to land use, zoning, and planning, and recommend appropriate actions in line with established protocols.
Issue infringement notices and enforce compliance where necessary, ensuring fairness and transparency.
Support the development and implementation of physical planning policies, processes, and procedures.
Maintain accurate records of inspections, assessments, enforcement actions, and related documentation.
Assist in research, data collection, and analysis for planning projects, including land use, transportation, and infrastructure assessments.
Collaborate with internal branches and external stakeholders, including developers, government agencies, and utility providers, to facilitate effective planning outcomes.
Respond to any other directions from the Physical Planner, Director, or City Manager in a timely manner.
Education & Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in urban planning, geography, or a related field. Master's degree an advantage
Membership with the Institution of Engineers PNG or other professional Institutions.
Driver’s License (minimum Class 3)
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge of urban planning, land use, infrastructure development, and regulatory compliance in the context of NCDC operations.
Understanding of the Physical Planning Act, Building Act, Land Act, Environment Act, and NCDC policies and processes.
Strong analytical, research, and data collection skills for assessing applications and planning projects.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Ability to conduct inspections, investigations, and enforcement actions with integrity and professionalism.
Proficiency in planning software, CAD tools, GIS, and Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple tasks under pressure.
Self-driven, disciplined, adaptable, and capable of working independently while supporting team objectives.
Commitment to ethical conduct, transparency, and advancing NCDC’s vision for sustainable urban development.
Work Experience
At least 3 – 5 years of experience in Physical Planning or related roles.

This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.

About the Role
The Child Adoption Liaison Officer
plays a key role in managing and coordinating the end-to-end adoption process, ensuring all administrative, legal, and logistical requirements are handled efficiently. The position works closely with families, legal entities, and social service providers to facilitate safe, transparent, and child-focused adoption outcomes.
Role Purpose
The purpose of this role is to oversee adoption processes by registering and assessing prospective adoptive parents, coordinating documentation, and ensuring compliance with legal frameworks. The role also supports the matching of children with suitable families while promoting adoption awareness and supporting adoptive parents throughout the process.
Key Responsibilities
Manage the full adoption process including registration, screening, matching, and post-adoption follow-ups
Ensure all adoption activities comply with PNG laws, policies, and child protection frameworks
Coordinate with legal entities, government agencies, and community stakeholders to facilitate smooth adoption processes
Maintain accurate, confidential records and prepare reports on adoption cases and trends
Deliver education and awareness programs on adoption processes and responsibilities
Monitor adoption cases, identify delays, and recommend process improvements
Provide logistical support including scheduling assessments, interviews, and related activities
Education & Qualifications
Grade 12 certificate PLUS a Diploma in Social Work, Community Development, Law, or or a related field is mandatory.
A bachelor’s degree in the above courses is the preferred qualification.
Certification in Child Welfare, Adoption Law, or similar is an advantage.
Drivers License is an added advantage (class 3 minimum)
Skills & Knowledge
Strong understanding of adoption laws, child protection frameworks (including Lukautim Pikinini Act), and legal procedures
Knowledge of case management, documentation, and data confidentiality practices
Ability to assess suitability of adoptive parents, including conducting interviews and home visits
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work with legal professionals, government agencies, and communities
Good communication and interpersonal skills, with sensitivity in handling emotional and complex cases
Ability to prepare detailed reports, manage databases, and track case progress
Understanding of child development and post-adoption support needs
Strong organisational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple cases and deadlines
Work Experience
At least 3–5 years of experience in social welfare, family law, or child welfare programs.
Experience in managing adoption cases or working with adoptive families is highly preferred.
Proven track record of collaborating with government agencies, legal professionals, and community stakeholders in child welfare programs.
Experience in conducting workshops or public awareness campaigns on family and child welfare topics.

The Senior Data and Records Officer
manages, analyses, and maintains community, census, and ward-level governance data for NCDC. The role ensures accurate data entry, record-keeping, and reporting, and works closely with GIS and City Data teams to integrate spatial information. By providing reliable and well-organised data, the officer supports informed decision-making and strategic planning across the Commission.
Role Purpose
The role exists to ensure that data collected from field operations is accurate, complete, and properly managed, enabling evidence-based decision-making. By maintaining digital and physical records, generating reports, and supporting GIS integration, the officer contributes to improved governance, planning, and service delivery.
Key Responsibilities
Compile, review, and enter data from field operations, including census, electoral rolls, and ward governance activities.
Maintain accurate, organised, and secure digital and physical records in line with NCDC policies.
Analyse and summarise data into reports, dashboards, and charts to support branch and Commission decision-making.
Collaborate with GIS and City Data teams to geocode, map, and integrate spatial information for planning and reporting.
Monitor data quality, identify gaps or inconsistencies, and recommend corrective actions.
Support internal requests, audits, and evaluations by providing timely and accurate data access.
Assist in resource management, including tracking data collection tools, digital assets, and supporting procurement documentation.
Provide technical guidance to field and internal teams on data collection, entry, and reporting processes

Minimum:
Certificate or Diploma in Information Management, Public Administration, Social Statistics, or a related field, plus a Grade 12 Certificate.
Preferred:
Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Information Management, Social Research, GIS, Data Science, or a related discipline. Additional training in data entry, data analysis, GIS systems, or records management is an advantage.
A valid Class 3 Driver’s Licence is desirable due to occasional travel to support field data collection

Strong knowledge of data management, analysis, and reporting practices.
Familiarity with GIS systems and spatial data integration.
Knowledge of records management, data privacy, and compliance standards.
Proficiency in database management, spreadsheets, and data visualisation tools.
Attention to detail, accuracy, and organisation when handling large volumes of data.
Ability to analyse trends, identify gaps, and provide actionable insights.
Strong communication and coordination skills for working across internal teams and external stakeholders.
Problem-solving skills to resolve data, technical, or system integration challenges.
Work Experience
Minimum 3–5 years of relevant experience in data entry, records management, statistical reporting, or GIS support.
Experience in summarising field data into useful reports and maintaining databases across multiple program areas.
Exposure to working with government, municipal authorities, or community-based organisations handling population or governance data is highly desirable.

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.

The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The Manager – Civil Survey & Design
leads NCDC’s Civil Survey & Design Branch, overseeing surveying, mapping, and civil engineering design functions that support infrastructure planning and delivery. The role ensures proposed road, drainage, and other civil projects are backed by accurate survey data, technically sound designs, and complete documentation. By translating infrastructure requirements into buildable designs, the Branch enables the Civil Projects Branch and other teams to implement works efficiently. The Manager collaborates closely with the Director – Engineering & Infrastructure and other engineering branches to ensure outputs align with NCDC’s engineering standards, capital works program, and infrastructure priorities.
Role Purpose
The role exists to manage survey and design activities, ensuring infrastructure projects are technically prepared, compliant with standards, and ready for procurement and construction. By providing strategic leadership, coordinating survey and design teams, and ensuring accurate technical documentation, the Manager supports effective project delivery, reliable infrastructure planning, and informed decision-making across NCDC’s engineering and civil works operations.
Key Responsibilities
Lead and manage all civil survey and geospatial data activities, ensuring accurate mapping, control points, and survey records to support planning, design, and project preparation.
Oversee the preparation and technical review of civil engineering designs, drawings, specifications, and documentation for roads, drainage, and other municipal infrastructure projects.
Coordinate survey and design outputs with internal branches, consultants, and project teams to ensure projects are technically ready for tender and implementation.
Provide technical advice on project planning, feasibility studies, design development, and construction implementation.
Ensure all designs and survey outputs comply with engineering standards, municipal regulations, and infrastructure design guidelines.
Maintain quality assurance practices for survey and design outputs, ensuring designs are practical, accurate, and constructable.
Plan and allocate resources for survey and design projects, including managing internal teams and external consultants as required.
Support project budgeting, procurement, and tender processes by providing cost estimates, Bills of Quantities, and technical documentation.
Foster a positive Branch culture aligned with NCDC values, including professionalism, integrity, collaboration, innovation, and service excellence.
Lead, mentor, and develop staff through regular performance reviews, activity planning, and professional development initiatives.
Perform other duties as assigned by the Director, Deputy City Manager, or City Manager.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Minimum: Bachelor in Civil Engineering, Surveying, or a closely related field from a recognised institution and Valid Driver’s License (min. class 3).
Preferred:
Bachelor’s degree as above, with additional certification or training in Civil Design, Geospatial Systems, Infrastructure Planning, or Project Management.
Eligible for membership as a Registered Engineer or Surveyor with the Institute of Engineers Papua New Guinea (IEPNG) or a recognised professional body.
Skills & Knowledge
Strong leadership and team management skills to guide survey and design staff in delivering accurate and timely outputs.
In-depth knowledge of civil engineering survey, mapping, and infrastructure design processes for roads, drainage, and urban development.
Ability to review and assess engineering designs, drawings, and technical documentation for accuracy, feasibility, and constructability.
Knowledge of engineering design standards, municipal regulations, and public procurement requirements.
Competency in project budgeting, preparation of technical documentation for tendering, and cost estimation.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills for effective coordination with internal teams, consultants, contractors, and regulatory authorities.
Analytical and problem-solving skills to assess site constraints, technical challenges, and provide practical engineering solutions.
Familiarity with geospatial data management, infrastructure planning, and technical coordination within municipal engineering contexts.
Proficiency in relevant engineering software, survey tools, and Microsoft Office Suite.
Commitment to NCDC’s values and goals, ensuring survey and design outputs support safe, effective, and sustainable infrastructure delivery.
Work Experience
Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in civil engineering design, infrastructure planning, surveying, or related technical roles.
Demonstrated experience leading engineering or survey teams and preparing technical documentation for infrastructure projects.
Experience working within government, municipal engineering departments, consulting firms, or infrastructure project environments is desirable.

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The Principal Legal Officer
leads NCDC’s Legal Branch and provides authoritative legal advice and guidance to the City Manager, Executive Management Team, and all Directorates. The role oversees litigation, prosecution, commercial advisory work, contract management, and representation before courts, tribunals, and statutory bodies. It also involves identifying and mitigating legal and reputational risks, contributing to policy development, and ensuring compliance with legislation, municipal by-laws, and governance standards.
Role Purpose
The role exists to ensure that NCDC’s operations, decisions, and regulatory actions are lawful, defensible, and compliant with applicable legislation and governance standards. By leading the Legal Branch, managing legal risks, and overseeing contracts, litigation, and advisory matters, the Principal Legal Officer supports effective governance and protects the Commission’s legal and reputational interests.
Key Responsibilities
Provide authoritative legal advice and guidance to the City Manager, Executive Management, Directors, and Branches to ensure lawful and defensible decision-making.
Lead and manage the Legal Branch, including planning, staff supervision, quality assurance of legal outputs, and operational management.
Oversee litigation, enforcement, and prosecution matters undertaken by or against the Commission, including managing external legal counsel.
Draft, review, and negotiate contracts, MoUs, leases, procurement agreements, and other legal instruments to protect NCDC’s legal and financial interests.
Conduct legal risk assessments and advise on mitigation measures to manage reputational and operational risks.
Ensure compliance with national legislation, municipal by-laws, regulations, and public sector governance standards.
Develop, implement, and maintain branch workflows, legal standards, and quality assurance processes.
Prepare legal reports, briefs, and opinions for the City Manager and Executive Management Team.
Coordinate with internal Directorates and external agencies to integrate legal considerations into project planning and operations.
Manage budget allocations, monitor legal expenses, and oversee procurement activities for the Legal Branch.
Maintain confidentiality, professional integrity, and adherence to ethical and legal standards in all legal matters.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Bachelor’s Degree in Law from a recognized tertiary institution and admitted to practice as a Lawyer in PNG with current Practising Certificate and active membership with the Papua New Guinea Law Society.
Preferred:
Desirable
: Postgraduate qualification in Law, Public Administration, Governance, or related field
Drivers license (Class 1)
Desirable
: Completion of recognised professional legal training or continuing professional development in areas such as: Commercial and contract law, Civil litigation and advocacy, Public sector governance and administrative decision-making.
Skills & Knowledge
In-depth knowledge of national legislation, municipal by-laws, regulations, and public sector governance standards.
Expertise in legal advisory, risk management, litigation, and prosecution processes.
Strong contract drafting, review, negotiation, and commercial advisory skills.

Job Title:
Construction Site Engineer
Reports To:
Projects Manager
Department:
Campus and Facilities Management
Location:
IBSUniversity, Mt. Eriama, 11 Mile Campus
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS) began its journey in 1987 as a modest initiative under Nades & Associates, primarily offering revision classes to support the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants, now known as CPA PNG. Over the past 36 years, IBS has grown steadily into a private university-level institution. Today, IBS is recognised as one of the largest business schools in Papua New Guinea, offering degree programmes in Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology. In addition, the institution continues to provide academic pathways for Grade 10 and 12 school leavers, as well as industry-recognised certification opportunities for experienced professionals seeking formal qualifications in their respective fields. This success has been made possible through the dedication and commitment of our team, whose collective efforts continue to make a meaningful contribution to Papua New Guinea by helping to educate and empower both current and future citizens.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but also enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
ABOUT THIS ROLE:
Construction Site Engineer will be responsible for overseeing all the activities on the construction site. The Construction Site Engineer ensures that projects are completed on time, with a budget, and our client’s specifications. This includes planning, coordinating, and supervising onsite functions, staffing, scheduling, and material control.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Execution of site work—Directing, executing, consulting, monitoring, quality controlling, and punch listing (rectifications) of relevant Civil Engineering construction works including earthwork, drainage work, road construction, and building construction (concrete and steel) along with incidental construction (curb laying, paving Interlocking concrete blocks, etc.).
Workplace Communications- Methods applicable to target groups, providing specific information to workers about their safety and developing team performances, commitment, and corporation.
Technical supervision during construction - Assess performances according to approved plans and drawings and consult the manager/professionals for any predicted problems and changes in the ongoing construction.
Supervise construction projects to ensure they are completed in line with the scope, time, budget, and set quality standards.
Ensure all work complies with building codes and safety regulations.
Inspect project sites regularly to identify and eliminate potential safety hazards.
Supervising and instructing the construction team as well as subcontractors
Communicating with clients’ suppliers, and laborers effectively
Prepare and submit progress reports.
Ensuring the quality of materials and workmanship meet specified standards and codes.
Manage the procurement of materials, machinery, tools and equipment necessary for the project.
Resolving conflicts or miscommunication that may happen onsite quickly and amicably.
Education and Qualification
Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of 5 years’ proven experience in a similar role.
In-depth knowledge of construction procedures, equipment, OSHA guidelines, and project management principles
Excellent organizational, leadership and management skills
Ability to communicate and report effectively.
Aptitude in Math and strong problem-solving skills
Good physical condition and stamina
Current state licensure for contacting or similar, if required
Exceptional attention to detail with an ability to spot potential risks or issues before they arise.
Application Process:
Interested candidates are invited to submit their resume, a cover letter, and relevant academic or professional certifications through the link provided.
https://ibs.bamboohr.com/careers/172
Apply

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.

First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners.

Position Overview:
The Assistant Lecturer in Business Management plays a pivotal role in delivering quality education and fostering the academic development of students in business-related disciplines. This position involves assisting with teaching, curriculum development, research, and mentoring, contributing to the overall success of the Business Management Course run at IBS College of TVET.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Teaching and Learning:
Assist in preparing and delivering lectures, tutorials, and workshops in Business Management and related subjects.
Facilitate interactive learning experiences to engage students and enhance their understanding of core business concepts.
Develop teaching materials, lesson plans, and assessment tools in collaboration with senior lecturers.
2. Curriculum Development:
Support the development and periodic review of the Business Management curriculum to ensure it meets industry and academic standards.
Integrate contemporary business practices, case studies, and trends into teaching content.
3. Student Support:
Provide academic guidance and mentoring to students to help them achieve their learning objectives.
Assess and evaluate students’ performance through assignments, projects, and examinations.
4. Research and Professional Development:
Participate in research activities and encourage student involvement in research projects.
Stay updated with current business trends, practices, and theories to inform teaching methods.
5. Administrative Duties:
Maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and assessment outcomes.
Contribute to departmental meetings, committees, and administrative tasks as required.
6. Community Engagement:
Support outreach programs, workshops, and seminars that promote business education.
Engage with local businesses and organizations to create partnerships and learning opportunities.
Qualifications and Experience:
Education:
A Bachelor’s degree in Business Management, Commerce, or a related field is essential.
A Master’s degree (or working towards one) in Business Administration or a similar discipline is highly desirable.
Experience:
At least 1–3 years of teaching or professional experience in business or management roles.
Prior experience in teaching at the tertiary or vocational education level is an advantage.
Technical Skills:
Knowledge of core business functions such as marketing, finance, management, HR management, and entrepreneurship.
Proficiency in using educational technology tools and learning management systems like Moodle and ERP
Soft Skills:

Access to modern teaching resources and tools.

26522.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
This role will manage supplier performance and provide the timely purchasing and procurement of goods delivered on time according to specified quantity, quality and cost requirements and within the supply policy guidelines.
This role will also be responsible to minimize the impact of the Section on the environment and ensure the workplace health & safety of employees, Contractors and other stakeholders are maintained
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Recommend sources for supply of goods and services, and obtain quotations from suppliers
Analyse quotes provided for quality against specification, price, timely delivery and innovation and select the best value supplier
Ensure purchasing at the optimal price in relation to quality, quantity and delivery method.
Issue Purchase Orders that follow K92 Mining policies and standards
Ensure appropriate documentation is completed and filed for all transactions.
Develop an understanding of the supply market and ensure well documented cost management.
Review performance of key suppliers across KPIs including price competitiveness, lead time compliance, delivery completeness & number of discrepancies.
Investigate invoice discrepancies to ensure suppliers are paid in a timely manner.
Investigate PO and goods receipt discrepancies to ensure that goods are available on site to meet requirements
Recommend procure to pay process improvements in conjunction with systems enhancements
Encourage site users to follow Supply processes and reinforce the correct process where required
Regular communication with internal customers to understand expectations and required timeframes when issuing purchase orders.
Follow up with suppliers to understand delays in quoting and seek alternative quotes as required
Ensure purchase requests are converted to purchase orders and issued to suppliers in a timely manner.
Manage out of hours purchase needs.
Communicate with suppliers to ensure that specified delivery timeframes are met.
Seek alternative suppliers, logistics solutions or substitute products where emergency requirements or supplier failure may lead to goods not being available on site on the date required
Participate in the planning of shutdown maintenance and project work to ensure the availability of goods during periods of unusual demand.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential and/or preferred that you:
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining values
Understanding of ERP systems (Pronto) to support purchasing processes.
Understanding of purchasing strategies, supplier evaluation and selection tools and their interaction with other supply processes.
Possess the ability to draft and compile quote request.
Possess Negotiation skills and understanding of negotiation techniques.
Understand Commercial analysis and evaluation.
Understanding total cost and life cycle costing.
Possess problem solving and decision-making capability.
Possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Have experience communicating with vendors in PNG and internationally
Possess the ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders.
Possess minimum 3 years’ experience in industry with relevant experience in transactional purchasing
Mining Industry experience preferred. Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

26789.description:
Office/ Division:
Office of the President
Position Title:
Director Public Relations
Position Number:
WPUEX005
Position Classification:
WPU Salary Grade 16
Job Location:
Ialibu, Western Pacific University Campus
Organzational Relationship
Reports to:
WPU President
Cordinates with:
Faultily Deans, Vice Presidents, Council Coordinating Officer, Academic Board Coordinating Officer, Cabinet Coordinating Officer, Staff Coordinating Officer, Students Coordinating Officer, Chaplain, Principal Legal Officer and Events Coordinator.
PURPOSE
The Director of Public Relations ensures the quality and consistency of and adherence to the University's brand and strategic plan when developing and overseeing marketing and public relations initiatives. The director participates in the development of materials for and the oversight of WPU’s Customer Relationship Management System. The director serves as the primary daily contact for brand awareness and strategy, issues management, and media relations, acts as the University spokesperson, and maintains relationships with key local, regional and national media. The success of this position ultimately depends on an ability to develop strong relationships, especially in the areas of enrolment marketing and recruitment. The director is responsible for leading the Office of University Public Relations and reports to the President.
DIMENSIONS
The Director for Public Relations will set and guide the strategy for all, marketing, digital communications and public affairs strategies. The Director for Public Relations will be responsible for planning and managing all communications messaging and activities, and building external relationships with all WPU’s stakeholders. The Director will work partner with senior colleagues within the University on a variety of strategic initiatives and collaterals to support WPU motto, vision, mission and objectives.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES
The Director will plan, implement and lead a global, integrated communications strategy for WPU that presents a consistent, compelling, and accurate account of the people and programs of the university to relevant audiences in the PNG and around the world. The content of communications will include written and spoken text, video, and other forms. The channels of communications will include live and remote presentations to live audiences, the WPU web site, traditional media, social media, and other forms;
Maintain effective administrative systems to ensure that accurate and attractive content is captured, developed, and presented consistently and efficiently using channels that will have maximum impact for each unit of time and money invested (often by presenting the same content through multiple channels);
Work with colleagues at WPU to ensure that WPU’s messages harmonize with and advance WPU’s overall communications strategy about its distinctive qualities starting with its global network, and to create new opportunities to tell WPU’s story in PNG and with key influencers across the international community;
The Director will serve as the spokesperson for the University. Day to day responsibilities.
Supervises all university communications accounts and activities; assure the meeting of departmental financial goals; and, maintains and develops staff;
Supports leadership communications;
Oversees the development and execution of public affairs, marketing, digital communications, social media and other communications strategies and programs to increase the visibility of the people and programs of the University;
Work with faculty to implement outreach strategies in support of their respective academic activities;
Supervises the writing of and edits press releases, articles, fact sheets, and backgrounders; cultivates media relationships; monitors responses to media requests, press conferences, media lunches and interviews, and special events;
Responsible for overseeing the development of presentations, reports, and fact sheets in support of leadership communications as well as the outreach activities of the University’s various administrative offices;
Responsible for ensuring “client satisfaction”;
Willingly take on other assignments from communications perspective that will assist WPU in realizing its vision and mission.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor's degree in Communications, Marketing or related field/experience required;
Demonstrated experience in Public Affairs, Marketing, Communications or related field, within both PNG and International environment.
Previous experience with Higher Education Sector or in an academic setting is desirable.
Excellent integrated marketing project management skills.
Ability to be detail oriented with excellent time management and organizational skills in order to develop priorities and meet deadlines.
Ability to collaborate and communicate effectively with various co-workers.
How to Apply

Expression of Interest
, including:

qualifications and certificates

supporting documents

one PDF file

26630.description:
Position Title:
Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer
Location: Port Moresby, National Capital District
Type: Full-time
Employing agency: Clinton Health Access Initiative Inc
Point of Hire: Port Moresby, National Capital District
BACKGROUND
The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:
http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
.
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.
Malnutrition remains a critical public health challenge in Papua New Guinea with severe malnutrition accounting for 10% of Paediatric hospital admissions and a case fatality rate of 12.4%
[1]
. Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life is a proven, cost effective and safe intervention to prevent malnutrition and its adverse effects. However, despite national efforts, the 2018 Demographic and Health Survey indicates that only 62% of children under six months in PNG are exclusively breastfed, highlighting gaps in early childhood nutrition practices
[2]
.
Madang District in Madang Province has been identified as a key project site for the Child Nutrition and Social Protection (CNSP) project due to its high rate of childhood malnutrition and limited access to essential health services. According to the Papua New Guinea Electronic Health Information System (eNHIS), the national target for moderate-to-severe malnutrition in children under five was set at less than 15% in 2023
[3]
.
However, Madang District reported a significantly higher malnutrition rate of 18.5 % in 2024, mirroring similar trends across Madang Province. The high burden of malnutrition stems from multiple interrelated factors, primarily the inability of families to provide adequate nutrition and the health system’s challenges in effectively engaging with communities on essential nutrition and child health interventions.
The inadequacy of health service delivery in Madang Province further exacerbates the malnutrition crisis. Outreach services remain low, with only seven integrated outreach sessions per 1,000 children under five years, limiting access to critical services such as immunization, growth monitoring, and nutrition counselling. Immunization coverage is alarmingly low at 21%, directly affecting vitamin A supplementation, which is essential for child growth and immunity. In addition, low antenatal care attendance of 47% for first visits and a facility-based delivery rate of only 32.1% further reduce opportunities for micronutrient supplementation during pregnancy, which is crucial for preventing maternal and child malnutrition. Addressing these service delivery gaps through targeted interventions will be key to improving child nutrition and overall health outcomes in Madang District.
Position Overview
The M&E Officer will lead the monitoring, evaluation, and learning efforts of the CNSP Project in Madang Province. This position plays a central role in tracking program performance, ensuring data-driven decision-making, and fostering accountability at all levels. The M&E Officer will be based in Port Moresby and report to the Special Advisor, Program Manager.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Design and implement a comprehensive M&E framework aligned with project objectives, CHAI internal systems, and donor reporting requirements.
Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) across program areas, including VHA performance, health facility engagement, and community mobilization.
Establish and manage project data systems including databases, data collection tools, reporting templates, and dashboards.
Conduct baseline, midline, and endline assessments to evaluate program outcomes, with specific attention to malnutrition rates, immunization coverage, and access to child health services.
Train Village Health Assistants (VHAs), health facility staff, and implementing partners on M&E tools, protocols, and standards.
Coordinate and supervise routine data collection, data entry, and quality assurance across 28 wards, 6 health facilities, and 5 aid posts.
Lead regular data quality assessments, site visits, and supervision to ensure data integrity and compliance.
Analyze program data and generate monthly, quarterly, and annual reports for CHAI, Provincial Health Authority, and donor stakeholders.
Prepare presentations, data visualizations, and briefs for internal and external use, highlighting key program trends and insights.
Support implementation of community-based monitoring tools such as the Community Scorecard and biannual household surveys.
Facilitate learning sessions and performance review meetings to discuss program progress, challenges, and evidence-based improvements.
Document best practices, lessons learned, and success stories for internal learning and external communication.
Monitor safeguarding indicators and community feedback mechanisms, including grievance reporting and PSEA compliance.
Support capacity building of PHA staff, VHAs, and local partners in M&E systems and practices.
Ensure alignment and integration with national health information systems, such as eNHIS.
Collaborate with government and development partners on harmonized monitoring strategies and shared learning platforms.
Any other responsibilities assigned by the Senior Program Officer and Special Advisor, Programs from time to time.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in public health, Statistics, Economics, Social Sciences, or a related field.
Atleast 5 years of relevant experience in M&E, preferably in maternal and child health, nutrition, or primary health care programs.
Strong skills in designing and managing M&E systems, conducting evaluations, and leading data collection efforts in rural settings.
Proficiency in statistical software (e.g., SPSS, Stata, R) and digital data collection tools (e.g., KoBo Toolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO).
Experience with database management, data visualization, and reporting tools.
Proven ability to present data clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience working with health systems or community health worker programs in PNG or similar contexts is highly desirable.
Excellent organizational, problem-solving, and communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (particularly Excel and PowerPoint).
Willingness to travel frequently to rural and remote communities.
Fluency in English and at least one local language is preferred.
HOW TO APPLY
Email Applications to:
[email protected]
Expiry Date: 19th April 2026
Apply

26668.description:
Superintendent – Metallurgy
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Metallurgy-Processing Department as a
Superintendent – Metallurgy.
Superintendent – Metallurgy (239661)
We seek to appoint an experienced Metallurgy Superintendent to join the Porgera team to lead metallurgical accounting and drive strategies that optimise plant performance and maximise gold recovery. This role has a strong development focus, with responsibility for knowledge sharing and future-proofing the metallurgy team in line with global best practice. It presents a unique opportunity to contribute to plant optimisation and improvements within an operation that values safety, visible leadership and operational excellence:
Duties and Responsibilities:
Leadership of the Metallurgy team to ensure safe, cost efficient, operation (daily to life-of-mine) is achieved through control and optimisation of the processing plant which includes Crushing, Grinding, Flotation, Pressure Oxidation autoclaves, Oxygen Plants, Lime Kilns, Tailings Detoxification, gold leach / CIP and gold room.
Accountable for high quality reporting of production, improvement and metallurgical reporting.  Including Metallurgical Accounting improvements.
Strengthen and enhance Metallurgy team performance and capability through focused training/coaching and feedback, employee development and talent identification / retention.
Hands on training, coaching and improvement of Metallurgical team members to ensure they understand the requirements of their roles, have strong analytical and reporting capabilities and they focus on transferring knowledge to operators to run the plant.
Establish and implement well-defined accountabilities for Metallurgy team interaction, reporting and support to process operations, assay laboratory, maintenance, mining, finance & product security teams.
Develop and manage systems to ensure training/employee development, statutory compliance and change management systems.
Manage and provide leadership of Project Management and Change Management processes to deliver capital and business improvement / continuous improvement projects to achieve business results, cost, quality, quantity and schedule.
Develop and manage processes for metallurgical assessment of future ore sources, improvements to process plant efficiency and reduction to operational risks.
Develop and manage systems to collect and analyse information to assess performance statistics, statutory requirements, systems efficiencies and business improvement initiatives, and provide timely recommendations for implementation in the operation.
To be suitable for this role, you will possess the following:
Tertiary Qualifications in Metallurgical or Chemical Engineering including at least 15 years’ experience in Minerals processing operations , including several years in Superintendent or senior metallurgist roles in the gold and / or base metals industry.
Demonstrated ability to identify, coach and mentor team members for their professional development and strengthen overall team capabilities in developing countries.
Demonstrated ability to lead a team safely and improve team safety awareness.
Demonstrated experience in management of metallurgical databases and accounting systems.
Demonstrated experience in project management, change management and business improvement systems to deliver results and act as a change agent
Experience in managing costs and budgeting
First aid certification or ability to obtain certification.
Certificate IV Training and Assessment (preferable).
Current Drivers Licence.
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures
Mobilisation Requirement
This is a PNG Citizen position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG citizens and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Superintendent – Metallurgy
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a
Superintendent – Metallurgy
. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

Labour Mobility Reintegration Technical Consultant
Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Job Description
Established in 1951, IOM is a Relate
Introduction
d Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is committed to ensuring a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally, while working towards harnessing the full potential of migration. Read more about IOM's workplace culture at
IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration
Nature of the consultancy: Advisory and technical services (Type A), subject to confirmation of funding and formal agreement with the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) of the Department of Treasury, providing strategic, analytical, and technical support to inform the design and potential operationalization of labour mobility reintegration systems, policies, and pilot programming in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
Project Context and Scope:
PNG has identified overseas labour mobility as a strategic pathway to expand employment opportunities, strengthen skills development, increase foreign exchange earnings, and improve household income and wellbeing. Labour mobility is coordinated by the LMU within the Department of Treasury, which oversees recruitment, deployment, worker welfare, return, and reintegration of PNG citizens under schemes such as the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) and Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) programmes.
As PNG’s participation in regional labour mobility schemes expands, the scale and complexity of return and reintegration have increased. Returned workers and their families experience interconnected economic, social, and psychosocial reintegration challenges, particularly in contexts of circular migration, family separation, limited job matching, financial pressures, and community expectations. Strengthening reintegration systems is therefore critical to ensuring that skills, savings, and overseas experience translate into sustained household resilience and national development gains.
Subject to confirmation of funding and a formal agreement with the LMU, this consultancy will support the proposed project “Supporting the Reintegration of Migrant Workers in Papua New Guinea,” to be implemented by IOM in alignment with, and complementary to, the Government-led Enhancing Labor Mobility from Papua New Guinea Project (ELMP) supported by the World Bank. The Consultant will provide technical and operational leadership for the design and implementation of reintegration components under this framework.
Organizational Department / Unit and Reporting
Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:
IOM Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion Unit, working in close coordination with the LMU, Department of Treasury, and the World Bank.
The Consultant will work under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission, IOM Papua New Guinea, with technical guidance from IOM Labour Mobility (Canberra) and the Regional Labour Mobility Specialist, IOM Regional Office in Bangkok. The Consultant will maintain close technical coordination with the LMU, Department of Treasury, and engage with the World Bank and other relevant partners, while collaborating with Regional Recruitment Hubs (RRHs), field teams, and subnational government counterparts to support coherent, government‑led implementation of labour mobility reintegration activities.
Responsibilities
Category A Consultants: Tasks to be Performed under this Contract
This is a Category A (Type A) consultancy providing senior technical and operational leadership to support implementation of labour mobility reintegration activities, in alignment with ELMP reintegration outputs and agreed delivery arrangements.
Reintegration Systems Design and Implementation Leadership
Lead the design, operationalisation, and technical oversight of labour mobility reintegration systems and programme components, aligned with ELMP reintegration objectives and national policy frameworks.
Provide technical and operational leadership to guide implementation of evidence‑based, family‑centred reintegration approaches through LMU and RRHs.
Support integration of reintegration considerations across the labour mobility cycle, including pre‑departure, overseas employment (including circular migration), and return.
Ensure safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, and psychosocial wellbeing considerations are embedded across reintegration systems and delivery modalities.
Evidence Generation, Monitoring and Learning
Lead reintegration evidence generation activities, including contextual analysis and validation exercises to inform implementation.
Support development and application of monitoring and learning frameworks for reintegration interventions, aligned with ELMP requirements.
Document implementation experiences, lessons learned, and good practices to inform adaptive management and future scale‑up.
Strategy, Programme and Systems Development
Provide technical leadership for the development and operationalisation of a nationally aligned Reintegration Strategy and Implementation Action Plan.
Translate strategic priorities into pilot‑ready programme designs suitable for decentralised delivery through RRHs.
Provide technical input into reintegration data management, referral, coordination, and tracking approaches between LMU and RRHs.
Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support
Design and deliver capacity‑building support for LMU and RRHs on reintegration case management, coordination, referrals, safeguarding, and engagement with returned workers and families.
Develop and contextualise a PNG‑specific reintegration training package drawing on regional and global good practices.
Provide on‑the‑job mentoring and technical backstopping to support consistent, government‑led reintegration implementation.
Coordination, Partnerships and Representation
Support coordination with government counterparts, development partners, and relevant stakeholders involved in labour mobility and reintegration.
Contribute technical inputs to inter‑agency discussions, workshops, and coordination fora related to labour mobility reintegration.
Support alignment between reintegration activities and broader ELMP implementation processes.
Reporting and Compliance
Provide technical inputs to inception, progress, and final reports related to reintegration implementation.
Ensure activities comply with IOM policies, safeguarding and data protection standards, and applicable environmental and social requirements.
4. Performance Indicators for the Evaluation of Results
Reintegration systems, tools, and programme components designed and operationalised in line with ELMP reintegration outputs.
Quality and timeliness of evidence products, strategy documents, and programme designs.
Strengthened institutional capacity of LMU and RRHs to lead reintegration implementation.
Documented lessons learned informing programme adaptation and scale‑up.
Timely and compliant technical contributions to project reporting.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications and Experience
Education
Master’s degree in Migration Studies, Development Studies, Economics, Public Policy, Social Sciences, or a related field; or
Bachelor’s degree with additional relevant professional experience.
Experience and Skills
Minimum five (5) years of progressive professional experience in labour mobility, migration governance, reintegration, or related programming.
Demonstrated experience providing technical and operational leadership for programme implementation.
Experience in evidence generation, strategy development, programme design, and capacity strengthening.
Experience working with government counterparts, UN agencies, and development partners.
Strong analytical, coordination, facilitation, and communication skills.
Experience in Papua New Guinea or comparable Pacific contexts is an asset.

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position.
Organizational Context and Scope
Papua New Guinea (PNG) has identified overseas labour mobility as a key pathway to expand employment opportunities, strengthen skills development, and improve household incomes. Labour mobility is coordinated by the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) within the Department of Treasury and implemented through a decentralised system of Regional Recruitment Hubs. Strengthening systems that support safe, well-managed migration across the full mobility cycle,  including preparedness, worker welfare, and sustainable reintegrationm remains a key Government priority, led by the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) in coordination with national stakeholders and partners.
In this context, IOM provides technical assistance, capacity strengthening, and operational support to Government counterparts to advance labour mobility initiatives in Papua New Guinea. This includes support to institutional coordination under the leadership of the LMU, reintegration analysis and planning, development of training approaches, and strengthening systems that promote sustainable outcomes for returning workers and their families.
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission, and in close coordination with national counterparts, the incumbent will provide administrative, coordination, and operational support to IOM’s labour mobility and reintegration programming, contributing to effective implementation of activities, strengthened collaboration with the LMU and partners, and alignment with national priorities and evolving labour mobility initiatives.

26742.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
At Newmont, safe and efficient port operations are critical to keeping our business moving. As Supervisor, Stevedoring, you will play a key role in overseeing day‑to‑day stevedoring and port activities at our Lihir operation, ensuring cargo movements are executed safely, compliantly, and efficiently. Through strong leadership and a focus on continuous improvement, you will directly contribute to operational reliability, workforce safety, and Newmont’s commitment to responsible operations.
As part of our team, you will
In this hands‑on role, you will:
Supervise stevedoring, port, and logistics operations to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable cargo handling and vessel activities.
Ensure full compliance with port regulations, safety protocols, and Newmont policies, actively promoting a strong safety‑first culture.
Coordinate and schedule daily port and logistics activities, allocating resources and tasks to meet operational priorities.
Conduct routine inspections of port facilities, equipment, and stevedoring activities to ensure operational readiness and compliance.
Administer and support regular safety audits of port operations, identifying areas for improvement and corrective action.
Liaise closely with other departments, contractors, and service providers to ensure seamless and efficient logistics coordination.
Monitor, collate, and report data on port and logistics performance, supporting accurate reporting and informed decision‑making.
Troubleshoot and resolve port and logistics issues, minimising disruptions to operations.
Prepare, induct, and guide new employees on port and logistics procedures, safety requirements, and ways of working.
Identify, assess, and manage operational risks, implementing mitigation measures and continuously monitoring risk exposure.
Lead by example, fostering a positive, collaborative, and safety‑focused team culture that encourages engagement and accountability.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To be successful, you will bring:
Demonstrated experience in stevedoring, port operations, transport, or logistics, with clear progression through roles of increasing responsibility.
Several years of experience working within port operations and stevedoring environments, with a solid understanding of applicable regulations and operational controls.
Proven capability in leading and developing operational teams, including day‑to‑day supervision, task allocation, and performance support.
Strong stakeholder engagement and customer service skills, with the ability to interact, influence, and resolve conflict with internal teams, contractors, suppliers, and service providers.
Sound understanding of project coordination, resource planning, risk management, and cross‑functional collaboration.
Practical experience across logistics and transport operations, including stevedoring activities, cargo movements, vessel scheduling and tracking, monitoring weather conditions, and managing loads to ensure safe and efficient port operations.
Demonstrated proficiency in data recording, tracking, monitoring, and reporting, with competent knowledge of KPIs and performance metrics.
Working knowledge of SAP systems, including data entry, tracking, and reporting relevant to port and logistics operations.
Solid understanding of health, safety, environment, and sustainability regulations and practices, with a strong commitment to safe operations.
Competent understanding of cost management and financial principles relevant to port and logistics operations.
Strong problem‑solving skills, applying practical judgement and continuous improvement thinking in a dynamic operational environment.
A current PNG driver’s licence, with the ability to work safely and effectively within an operational port setting.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) day shift roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea. You will join a dynamic operational port environment. You will work closely with cross‑functional teams, contractors, and service providers, supporting round‑the‑clock operations where safety, teamwork, and clear communication are essential to success.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of a global mining leader committed to safety, integrity, sustainability, and inclusion. We offer:
A strong safety‑first culture where people come first
Opportunities to lead meaningful work that keeps critical operations running
Support for learning, development, and career progression
A collaborative environment where diverse perspectives are valued
If you are an experienced stevedoring or port operations professional looking to step into a leadership role with impact, we encourage you to apply.

About Hastings Deering
Hastings Deering is one of the top 5 Caterpillar dealerships globally. We sell, rent, and offer support and parts distribution services for Cat® products across a range of industries, including resources, general construction, civil transport and commercial construction, power systems, government, primary industries and marine.
We have more than 3,500 employees across 23 business service centres throughout Queensland, Northern Territory, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and New Caledonia, with our headquarters based in Brisbane, Australia.

Hastings Deering is on the hunt for a motivated
Technical Trainer with strong Operator-Trainer capability
. In this role, you will not only develop and deliver technical training programs but also utilize your practical experience operating Caterpillar machinery to coach and demonstrate safe, productive operating techniques. Your background in the mining sector and commitment to continuous improvement will support high‑quality outcomes for our internal teams and customers.
